checks.why: <a itemprop="author"> yields its href, so the value is '/authors/OL26320A/J.R.R._Tolkien; /authors/OL26320A/J.R.R._Tolkien' -- a path, twice. The author's name as written is not recovered. Same root cause as the Gutenberg creator field.
<a itemprop="publisher"> yields '/publishers/Metis_Yayıncılık'. The readable publisher name is in the link text and is discarded.

The title the URL and the page heading use is NOT inside the Book scope as an itemprop, so no record names it. A query about The Lord of the Rings that retrieves this line gets a 4.45 attached to a Turkish edition title and a bare type.

A GAP. `author` is a LIST of Person objects. The list branch only keeps SCALAR members; object members are pushed out as child records, and a Person whose only keys are `name` (the record's own name) and `url` (skipped) has no fields, so it is not emitted. One author object folds onto the parent line (see wikipedia-schema-org); three do not. The three names are in the page prose here, so nothing is lost on THIS page -- the asymmetry is the finding.
DEDUPE, correct: the prose names Our World in Data within the proximity window.

A GAP, not a dedupe -- the string appears nowhere in the extracted text. `publisher` here is an Organization that also carries a nested `logo` object. The folding rule requires the nested object to have no nested values of its own, so a publisher WITH a logo is pushed out to a child record; that child's only remaining key is its name, which is the record's name, so it has no fields and an unnamed-depth record with no fields is not emitted. Compare ourworldindata.org/energy, whose publisher carries `logo` as a plain STRING and therefore does fold onto the line. Same schema, opposite outcome, decided by the type of a field this module skips.

`sameAs` is on the skip list. `mainEntity` -- the SAME URL under a different key -- is not, so the identifier does reach the line once. Deliberate to record: the skip list is key-based, so an identifier's survival depends on which key a publisher chose for it.
DEDUPE: the rendered page prints v3.0.5 beside the title.

`^url$` is on the skip list by design. Worth recording because this URL is NOT the URL that was fetched -- the record points at a later version of the deposit -- so the skip also suppresses a real inconsistency between the record and the page it sits on.
